sentences.text: Belantsea possessed a unique appearance that resembled a bony fish rather than a cartilaginous one.
The name Belantsea honors a legendary ancestor of the Crow Tribe.
The genus Belantsea was described by Lund in 1989.
Fossils of Belantsea montana were found in the Bear Gulch Limestone lagerstätte, a site preserving exceptional fossils.
Researchers think Belantsea was adapted for living in sponge reefs based on its body shape.
Belantsea likely ate hard-shelled marine invertebrates, indicated by its few large triangular teeth.
Its diet included ancient sponges, brachiopods, crinoids, crustaceans, and small fish.
Belantsea belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
The animal is part of the family Belantseidae.
The species Ctenopetalus occidentalis is a synonym of Belantsea occidentalis.
Belantsea lived during the Lower Carboniferous period.
The genus lived from the Lower Carboniferous to the Upper Permian.
Belantsea lived between 326.9 and 264.9 million years ago.
Belantsea went extinct during the Permian-Triassic mass extinction.
